thread:
marta: Quick follow-up on the RFC about carving out a thin 'service surface' for orchestration (validation, auth, routing) from the runtime-heavy path. Want to align on tradeoffs + migration steps.

ajay: +1 saw the RFC, main question is the latency impact of an extra hop. do we have microbenchmarks? :thinking_face:

leo: We ran a quick sim last week — adding a surface layer + HTTP hop is ~4-7ms median on our env but p95 moves by ~20ms if we don't batch properly. batching and async KV lookups matter.

sophia: Can we keep the current internal API and introduce the surface as a proxy with feature flags? that avoids immediate client changes.

marta: That's the plan: proxy-in-front model initially, feature flags for routing to new surface. Then migrate consumers once stable. need to lock the interface contract before we start.

chris: Interface proposal (from RFC):
```
POST /v1/serve
{ "model": "<id>", "input": "...", "session_id": "...", "meta": {...} }
```
Response includes location token for streaming. keep it thin — no session ownership semantics in surface.

devon: If surface is thin, where does session lifecycle live? runtime still owns KV and eviction rules, right?

leo: yes runtime keeps session and KV cache ownership. surface only validates, enriches headers, does tenant auth and routing. all cache hits go straight to runtime after routing.

pm-olivia: Need to capture compatibility and rollout plan for customers on Dedicated/Private. They may be running pinned versions. migration needs opt-in + clear release notes.

ajay: tradeoffs:
- Pros: smaller attack surface, faster iteration on routing/auth, clearer ownership
- Cons: extra hop, more cross-service contracts, potential for subtle latencies under load

marta: Proposed migration steps: 1) implement surface as proxy behind a feature flag + compatibility layer (2 sprints), 2) run canary for 2 weeks with 10% traffic and observability hooks (p95, error-rate, token-cost deltas), 3) iterate on batching/async lookup to keep p95 within SLO, 4) flip route and decommission monolith hook (1 sprint), 5) post-mortem and tech-debt ticket sweep.

sophia: Observability: we need new per-request tags: route_variant, surface_latency_ms, runtime_latency_ms, kv_hit_bool. Also add end-to-end trace id and ensure sampling keeps tail traces.

infra-bot: New feature flag created: ff/orchestration_surface_alpha.owner=marta

chris: Can we have an automatic fallback where surface can proxy-back to monolith if runtime returns overload? i.e. surface has fallback policy to route to legacy path on capacity signals.

leo: yes implement policy table: prefer-runtime -> on overload -> legacy-fallback. fallback must be visible in metrics.

devon: estimated effort: coding + infra ~3 sprints, testing + canary 1 sprint, cleanup 1 sprint = ~5 sprints. plus 2 sprints buffer for unexpected perf work. total ~3 months.

pm-olivia: prioritization: we align this with the Q3 tech-debt plan. can we get a quick ROI doc showing operational savings and reduction in cognitive load for runtime teams?

marta: I'll draft a one-pager for exec + ROI numbers (expected decrease in runtime incident mean time by isolating auth/routing; easier experiments on routing). assigning owners: marta (product/arch), ajay (perf lead), leo (runtime lead), chris (platform infra).

ajay: next steps: perf microbench this week, prototype proxy with header enrichment, add metrics hooks. I'll post raw numbers in this thread by Friday.

leo: ack. if numbers look good we'll open a migration board and schedule the first sprint.

pm-olivia: add a stakeholder review with security (auth path), legal (if any API contract changes for customers), and solutions engineering for Dedicated customers before canary.

marta: noted. thanks all. I'll update RFC with this migration plan and owners. :raised_hands:
